utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The protections for the next witness which have been applied for will be granted. While we're waiting for the witness, I will deal with some administrative matters dealing with hearings at the end of November and the beginning of December. The week commencing Monday the 24 of November contains a UN holiday on Wednesday the 26th of November. To accommodate this, the hearings that week will be on Monday the 24th of November, Tuesday the 25th of November, and Thursday the 27th of November. Judge Robinson will not be able to attend the hearings on Tuesday the 25th and Thursday the 27th of November for medical reasons; therefore, Judge Kwon and I will be sitting alone on those days under the Rule. In the week of Tuesday the 2nd to Thursday the 4th of December, the hearings will take place as usual on Tuesday to Thursday, but Judge Robinson, for the same reason, cannot attend those hearings, and Judge Kwon and I will sit alone. In the week commencing Monday the 8th of December, there is a Plenary meeting of the Judges and therefore there will be no hearings on those days. That is Thursday the 11th and Friday the 12th of December. The Trial Chamber will therefore sit that week on the days of Monday the 8th to Wednesday the 10th of December. Yes. Is there anything before the witness comes in?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just two preliminary matters, Your Honour. I will not be seeking to lead any evidence in closed session. I would ask that if the amici or the accused wish to inquire about the specific position that this gentleman held in the municipality, that that be done in closed session. I'd also ask that his -- his wife and his daughter were both subjected to prolonged and extremely grievous sexual abuse. I would ask if that is going to be inquired into that that be done, out of respect for those family members, that that be done in closed session. And I would ask that a binder containing three exhibits be assigned a number at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. And I understand there is a matter of a ruling under Rule 92 bis in relation to this witness which has not been dealt with. In fact, we had made the ruling but no written form had appeared. That will be granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And we will have the exhibit number, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 566, Your Honour, with tab 1, 2, 3 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, you have been granted -- sir, you have been granted protective measures pursuant an order of the court. You will therefore be referred to as B-1122 during the course of your testimony here. I would ask you to begin your testimony by taking a look at tab 1 of Exhibit 566 and tell us whether you recognise that document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that your name at the top of that document and is it also a brief summary of your professional and educational background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you now to take a look at tab 2 of that document. It is a two-part document, an English translation of a statement and a statement in the B/C/S language. Do you recognise whose statement that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. It's my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And after coming to The Hague, did you review that statement and notify the Office of the Prosecutor of some corrections that you wished to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to look at tab 3 of that binder, Exhibit 566, and ask you, is that an addendum to your statement, making several corrections to your original statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to return to tab 2, page 11, and my question to you is: Is that your signature on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you initial every page of that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you verify the truthfulness and the accuracy of that statement here now being a sworn witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask you to once again turn to tab 3 and if you would look at the second page in tab 3. Is that also your signature to the addendum of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And now being a sworn witness, do you verify the truthfulness and accuracy of that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, pursuant to Rule 89(F), I would tender both tabs 2 and 3 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just help us with the atlas so we can find this. I think this is the first witness from this municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, my apologies. I don't have our copy of the atlas here. Perhaps I could ask the witness to explain where geographically Gacko is located and then I'll have a page reference for the Chamber at the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask you to describe for the Chamber where Gacko is located in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. Gacko is in Eastern Herzegovina. The neighbouring municipalities are to the north Foca and Kalinovik, to the east Montenegro, to the south Bileca and Stolac, and to the west Nevesinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, the Chamber is in possession of your statement which is a full account of the events as you witnessed them in Gacko. I want to ask you some specific questions regarding that evidence. The first question I would like to ask you is: In your statement, you describe the presence of White Eagles in Gacko, and could I ask you to identify the earliest period in time when you saw White Eagles, members of the White Eagles in Gacko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: It was in March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the atlas reference is page 33, sector D3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And sir, how were you able to identify them as White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: They wore the White Eagle insignia on their sleeve here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, during the course of the time that they were in Gacko, can you describe or did you form an opinion with respect to the relationship between the White Eagles and official members of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, you see, when the White Eagles arrived in Gacko, they were quartered in the barracks 3 kilometres to the east of Gacko, and these were barracks used by the Yugoslav army. And then we could see them socialising in town, going to cafes together. I think they acted together Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. as far as we could see, completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you make any observations with respect to the weapons that were carried by these members of the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, I did. They wore -- they carried Yugoslav army weapons, mostly automatic rifles. They also had heavy weapons, mortars. They had guns. One could see that when they went off to the Mostar battlefield. They had uniforms and all the logistics of the JNA, and this was obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to jump ahead to a meeting that you describe in your statement on the 28th of April, 1992, a meeting that was held with General Momcilo Perisic. Can I ask you to summarise to the Chamber what, if any, assurances the Muslim community sought from General Perisic; and secondly, what assurances did he give the Muslim community?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I remember there was a meeting of representatives of the Serb and the Muslim peoples, and this meeting was also attended by General Perisic, who was commanding operations near Mostar. In view of the fact that some events had taken place in Gacko, violent events against the Muslims, the Muslims asked General Perisic to guarantee that he would protect the civilian populations. There were only civilians there. General Perisic addressed the meeting promising this, and the representatives of the Muslim side asked about the paramilitary formations. They asked who the White Eagles were and what they were doing in Gacko, because General Perisic said that in his area of responsibility, he would not tolerate any sort of paramilitary organisations. When he was asked about the White Eagles and who they were, he didn't give a reply, but he did promise to protect the civilian population in the area of Gacko. However, he failed to keep his promise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the day after General Perisic said that he would not permit paramilitaries in the area, what, if anything, happened to the members of the White Eagles in Gacko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I know that representatives of the Bosniak side told General Perisic about the activities of the White Eagles, and on the following day, the White Eagles went to the Mostar front, and on their way through the town, they started firing wildly on the main square. They fired shots, a lot of shots, and then they went to the Mostar front. I don't think that they stayed in Mostar long, only about a week. And after that, they came back to Gacko, and again they were quartered in the barracks, the military barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So the day after General Perisic addressed the combined Serbian and Muslim communities, the White Eagles left for a period of about a week before returning to Gacko; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, if I can draw your attention to the 1st of June, 1992. Your statement refers to another meeting, a meeting with Colonel Parezanin of the JNA. Can I ask you to summarise for the Chamber what it was Colonel Parezanin said to the people assembled or people present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: On the 1st of June, 1992, arrests of the Bosniak population in Gacko began, and on that day there was another meeting between representatives of the Serbs and Muslims or, rather, Bosniaks, and in the morning, this was in the Municipal Assembly, and in the afternoon in the police headquarters. While the meeting was going on, a gentleman came in and said he was Colonel Parezanin. I think he was assistant of the corps commander for the rear. The topic of the negotiations was that the Serbs wanted the Muslims to give up some weapons which they didn't have, and Colonel Parezanin said, "Discuss this with the official authorities and fulfil your promise, otherwise I will raze this Muslim village to the ground," and he pointed to a Muslim village, and then he left the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when he returned and introduced another person who was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. When he reached the door, he turned back and said, "I forgot to introduce this gentleman." And there was a man sitting there whom I didn't know, and he said, "This is Colonel -" and I forgot his name, but he said he was the commander of the Red Berets. This was the first time I had heard of the name Red Berets. This gentleman said, "Yes, I am" such-and-such a person, "fulfill the requirements of the Serbian side. If not, I can bring 5.000 specials here." And then I think they both left the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, the witness said, as far as I can interpret what he said in Serbian, that they were to fulfil the promises and that he was able to raze to the ground a hill over there, and the witness said there was also a Muslim village there. The record says, as it was interpreted, "Fulfil your promises or I will raze this Muslim village to the ground." So the interpretation is completely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us -- let us -- we needn't -- We needn't go on further but we will clarify what it was the colonel said. Can the witness do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I can assist. The colonel addressed us and asked us to fulfil the demands of the Serbian side, and if we failed to do this, he said, "I am able to raze that hill to the ground," but there were Muslim villages on that hill. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now return not to Colonel Parezanin but the other colonel whose name you do not recall but who was introduced as the commander of the Red Berets. My question to you is: Was he wearing at that time any type of red headgear that you could see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When he made this reference to 5.000 specialists, what was your understanding of what a "specialist" was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I didn't know who the Red Berets were, to be quite honest. I didn't know who they were. At that moment, we were under enormous pressure. It was a very unpleasant situation and I took this seriously.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you know what he meant when he referred to the term "specialist"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Probably a Special Purpose Unit. It was afterwards that I learned who the Red Berets were. They were a special unit from Nis, of the JNA. At that moment, I didn't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: From what source did you learn this information about where the Red Berets came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well -- well, you find out. People talk. You ask people. In communication with other people. So I didn't learn it from any official source. We were simply struggling to survive at that time, to save ourselves somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. 1122, you say in your statement that prior to the elections -- and you're talking about the elections in Bosnia-Herzegovina, I assume; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that in the time that preceded those elections, the SDS, the Serbian Democratic Party -- you say that in paragraph 4. "In the time leading up to the elections, the SDS held large rallies in Kosovo and Belgrade and other places." Were they rallies of the Serbian Democratic Party, in fact? When you say, "Many Serbs from Gacko attended these rallies and they were strong Serb nationalists." That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, that is in the statement. However, I corrected that subsequently and said that during the time the elections -- during the time large-scale rallies in Kosovo and Belgrade were taking place, and other places, that a large number of nationalists from Gacko, from the Serbs, attended and went to attend those events. So I made this correction in the addendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. 1122. Now, these large-scale rallies at Gazimestan Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and Usce, did you hear a single word said at Gazimestan or Usce which could be qualified as being nationalistic or nationalism?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, I think that the contents and subject of those rallies is common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So your answer is in fact yes; you're claiming that it is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In that brief examination-in-chief, and I'm not going to present you with all the different rallies because we'd use up a lot of time that way, but tell me this, please: Did you see the rallies of the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the first nationalist party that was established in Bosnia-Herzegovina was precisely the Democratic Party of the SDA on the 26th of May, 1990? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I really don't know the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know the dates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No, I don't. The SDA, the SDS, the HDZ, I really don't know when they were formed, but I do know about the local level in Gacko. I know that the Serbian Democratic Party was set up on the 2nd of August, for example, 1990, whereas on the 1st of September, the Party of Democratic Action was formed. So I just know this at a local level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now tell me what the rallies were like of the SDA party, the Party of Democratic Action. What were their rallies like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: They were pre-electoral activities, in fact, where the political parties or, rather, the political party, the Party of Democratic Action, the SDA, tried to win over the electorate in order to gain power, come into power, and this was in fact a power struggle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, did you at those rallies notice any exclusiveness in the positions taken by the Party of Democratic Action that was expressed in the fact that there was room in Bosnia only for Muslims and nobody else, or anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No. That was never the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It was never the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No. It wasn't even in the programme of the Party of Democratic Action at all. It wasn't set out there either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, is it true and correct that the basis for the party's activities was the Islamic declaration by Izetbegovic, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I'm not informed in that respect, so I can't answer your question. I haven't read the Islamic declaration either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You haven't read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No, I haven't, quite certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And yet you were an SDA functionary, official.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I think that's got nothing to do with it. If I was an official, I still didn't have to read the declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, you say in paragraph 4 that there was propaganda which promoted Serb nationalism and invented crimes which the Muslims were supposed to have committed against the Serbs and that some articles mentioned Gacko and invented incidents and crimes which the Muslims were supposed to have committed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: That's how my statement reads, and that's the truth of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So was that remembrance of history? Is that what this is referring to, when Islamism was being revived and with respect to the breakdown of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: When I gave this statement, this referred to what was going on in Gacko, and it was a revival or burgeoning of Serb nationalism, because literary evenings were being held which did not resemble literary evenings at all, in fact. They represented political manifestations. And then I have in mind the guslevski evenings which were characteristic for the area. Mr. Milosevic, you know that through that that is a good way of reviving nationalism. Then I also have in mind the important people that came to Gacko to make speeches, who weren't from the area originally, who didn't live in Gacko but who at one time originated from Gacko. And I also have in mind the books that had a highly negative effect in the area and revived and garnished nationalism. Vuk Draskovic's book is a case in point, called Noz, or The Knife.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. 1122. You wrote all this in point 4, and you've just stated that they were writers who lived in Belgrade or elsewhere but originated from the area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Not only authors; I mention important people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mention Gojko Djogo, you mention Vuk Draskovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you have particularly highlighted Draskovic's book. And as far as I know, all that came out far before these events took place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, but it was a good topic, a good subject for the nationalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the events which are described in the book were actually based on historical facts, on events which took place? And the -- and the book was published much before any of these events took place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I think that this is a very vulnerable area, region, and whenever the situation was unstable in the region, then there were things on both sides, inhumane acts, killings, crimes, they did take place, but far more on the Serb side than the Bosnian side, and history proves that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean in World War II?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Before World War II as well and in the Second World War also.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you're explaining -- as you've just mentioned the guslevski evenings, for those of you who are not familiar with this term, the gusle were a national instrument to accompany folksongs that were being sung; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And these are folksongs that have been sung for centuries and decades; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. But it is a time when exclusively nationalist songs are sung, and that's the subject, that's the topic of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the gusle, the instrument the gusle, a string instrument, contributed to the development of nationalism. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you count the gusle evenings among the nationalist manifestations and events that took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Absolutely so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. 1122. If the people whose ancestors originated from the area or have relations there, have houses there, if they came to the area, if they were authors, public personages, took part in the various cultural events or whatever you like to term them, what has that got to do with Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I remember very well a meeting held by the Serbian Democratic Party in Gacko at which Budimir Kosutic took the floor, and he just originated from Gacko, but he was very close to the SPS party and your own party, very close to your own party. And he made a speech there, and it was quite obvious what the subject and goal of what he was saying was. That was quite evident. We knew what he was saying, what the subject was, what it was geared towards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know that Budimir Kosutic is a professor at the faculty of law in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you said that Budimir Kosutic, he wrote down that Budimir Kosutic was my chef de cabinet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: That's how he introduced himself, and I think that he took part in television programmes in that capacity fairly frequently, Yugoslav television, the former Yugoslavia television. He would be on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. 1122, he quite certainly couldn't have appeared in that capacity because he never worked in my cabinet, let alone the fact that he was the -- my chef de cabinet. Throughout the time that you're referring Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to he was in actual fact a professor of law at the Faculty of Law. So what you're saying that he introduced himself on television as being my chef de cabinet is quite untrue. He couldn't have introduced himself as being that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Depends on what the man said on television. Whether he was telling the truth or not is an another matter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. May, can you imagine a law professor coming on television, known by so many people, and saying, "I am President Milosevic's chef de cabinet"? That is nonsense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, law professors can say a great many things, but let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you there. I quite agree, yes. That is true for men of the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Anyway, Mr. 1122, isn't -- wasn't that equally true both for the Serbs and the Muslims and for the Croats, for the Macedonians, the Slovenes, that regardless of where they lived, they always have some connections with their roots, with their region of origin? They would go back from time to time to take part in certain activities. It wasn't specific to Gacko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, his speech there was full of nationalism, and his speech wasn't suited to this kind of event, an event held by people who wanted peace. It served to burgeon nationalism.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when did Budimir Kosutic deliver that speech?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: It was an event, a manifestation. I can't remember the exact date. It was sometime, I think, in the autumn of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was it a cultural event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No. It was a political event of the party of -- of the Serbian Democratic Party, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it was a meeting of the Serbian Democratic Party. Was Kosutic a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: This is how it was: It was a manifestation of the SDS party in Gacko, and at that event there were many speakers. One of them was Budimir Kosutic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, I don't have Kosutic's speech here with me, and I don't think we need discuss his speech at all either with you, that is, but as in point 10 you say that the first large scale rally of the SDS was held on the 2nd of August, 1990, in the village of Nadanici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Nadanici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right, Nadanici. I don't know the names of those places in that region. Anyway, it was organised by the church and it was held in front of the church, and it was held on the date of an Orthodox holiday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, do you have an explanation as to what was happening there? Now, if the church organises for an Orthodox religious holiday, a rally of citizens, Serbs who are of the Orthodox faith, to have them meet in front of the church for an Orthodox holiday, what about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, the Orthodox holiday of the 2nd of August is well known as Ilindan, St. Ilija's Day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, everybody knows that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: And on that day, on St. Elijah's Day, there was a traditional festival that was held, but that particular day, St. Elijah's Day was used to set up the Serbian Democratic Party, and it was from the SDS headquarters, I think, that Velibor Ostojic was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Velibor Ostojic was from the headquarters in Sarajevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So they were there for St. Elijah's Day and they formed the SDS branch of Gacko; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, was that after the SDA party had been formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No. It was before the SDA party had been formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean in Gacko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: After the SDA had been set up throughout Bosnia. I assume you know that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, in Gacko, the SDA party was formed on the 1st of September of that same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in Gacko it was formed 28 days before the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: After.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. After the party in Gacko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: The SDS was established before it was established first in Sarajevo and then in Gacko later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now in addition to the SDA, was there a Muslim, the MOS branch of the SDA party, the youth Muslim organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You didn't have a Muslim youth alliance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No. There were only 3.800 Muslims in Gacko at that time, and our only goal was to survive, to save our heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you know nothing about this Muslim youth alliance. You have no experience with that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No, I know nothing about it, I have no experience of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So I'm not going to ask you anything about that then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in Gacko with respect to the elections in 1990, the autumn of 1990, in fact, when the elections were held, establish a coalition of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You were independent, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, there were three political parties at the elections; the SDS, the SDA, and the SDP. Those three parties had their list of candidates, their ticket.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The HDZ, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, there were no Croats there, no Croat inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: SDP is the Social Democratic Party; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me this now, please: How come or how was it that the distribution was made? How were the positions and posts after the elections distributed in your municipality? Was this done on the basis of a proportionate ratio, Serbs/Muslims? And I'm referring to point 8 of your statement, because you say that the SDS held all the influential positions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that none of the SDS members could act independently. What about the secretary for national defence? Was he Safet Skaljic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he was in charge of defence on behalf of the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: He was chief of the Territorial -- the chief of Territorial Defence was a Serb, and he was the next man. He was the administrative man and had an administrative post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he was the municipal defence secretary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No. There was a chief there and the structure was quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And Elvedin Zugur, the police chief, was he also from the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, he was on paper, but he wielded no influence whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, how could a police chief not wield any influence if he is in command of the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: We wasn't in command of the police because the deputy police chief was a Serb, Branko Popic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the commander, the chief, was a Muslim and the deputy a Serb, is that it, on paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: On paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: May I be allowed to explain? The mayor of the municipality was a Serb. The Prime Minister was a Serb. The chief of MUP was a Serb. The Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. commander of the Territorial Defence was a Serb. So those were the key positions in the municipal organs. Anything underneath that, below that -- the chief of police comes below the chief of MUP, for instance. So in actual fact, they were just figureheads, directors of companies, for example, general managers. There were some Muslims before but there were none afterwards. The Serbs took all key positions. I don't know that there was a single Muslim director except in the hospital when he was replaced by a medical technician whereas he had the title of "primarius" before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the defence secretary, Safet Skaljic, from the SDA and the chief of police, Elvedin Zugur, from the SDA as well, they did hold those posts. You're not challenging that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in the police structure generally were there Muslim policemen, as many, for instance, as there were Muslims in the municipality, proportionate to the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, until the SAO, the Serb autonomous region of Herzegovina was formed, and then the Muslim policemen left the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So they left it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, because they weren't given any tasks to do. They were just figureheads. They had no power.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You say in point 10 that when the conflict in Croatia started, the Serbs organised a "Jurisni Bataljon," an attack battalion, which was a name used by a Chetnik unit in World War II.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can any atrocities, as you say, committed by the Serbs be compared to the atrocities committed against the Serbs in World War II? There is a mass grave there, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, but this mass grave was called Dizdarusa previously, and a large number of Muslim families were slaughtered, many of them called Dizdaruvic, which is why the place was called Dizdarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In 1941 were Serbs thrown into this pit, into this ravine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I read about this but I wasn't alive at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, no, you weren't alive in 1918 and yet you're pointing out this answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I'm saying that this was a vulnerable area where many atrocities were committed on all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how many Serbian women and children were thrown into this ravine in World War II?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I really wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that the SDA called on soldiers and officers born in Bosnia to leave the JNA, and at the same time they prevented the calling up of JNA soldiers from Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Where did I say this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'll find this for you. It's in paragraph 9. The last third of this paragraph: "We discussed the mobilisation call in this manner and made a recommendation that SDA did not have to answer the mobilisation call. We stated that the war in Croatia and Slovenia was not our war, and that we would join the effort when the borders of our municipality were attacked. Therefore no Muslims joined the mobilisation."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. This is quite true. We did not sign a document with the SDA or, rather, there was an inter-party commission of the SDS and SDA where the SDA said they did not want to join in this conflict because we were not in favour of war. We were in favour of peace. This was not our war, and we said that we would go to war when our municipality was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but as you know, the JNA was the armed force of all the peoples of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: All this was taking place, I think, after Bosnia and Herzegovina was internationally recognised. No, no. This was 1991, so you're right. Yes, that's correct. We did not respond to the mobilisation; correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the JNA attempted to prevent the conflict and that was its main role precisely at the time when you refused to join the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know that the SDA continuously de-legitimised the armed forces and that this was one of your standpoints, that the JNA should be abandoned, that the mobilisation should not be responded to, and that the Muslims should boycott the JNA in every way? Do you remember when the SDA proclaimed its own war command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No. No, I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did the SDA party say that the Territorial Defence Staff was pro-Serb and an occupying army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: General Gosaluvic [phoen] was the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. All I know is that he was the commander of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then he was replaced and the Territorial Defence Staff was disbanded and their own staff was set up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I was hiding in the mountains at the time when this happened in Sarajevo, so I'm not familiar with the details. At that time, I was in the wilderness, in the mountains in Zelengora with my children and my wife, trying to save our lives. So I was not able to follow the events that were taking place then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you were not able to follow these events, I won't ask you about them. Somebody else will probably be able to say more about this. You say that the weapons of the Territorial Defence were stored in your area and that in 1989 the republican authorities decided to move these weapons from Gacko to Konjic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: That's how it was in all municipalities in 1989. The weapons were taken to central depots. So they were taken to Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: To keep them safe there; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, but three truckloads were separated off - I don't know under what regulations - and brought to Gacko and distributed to the Serbs, and they were trained to use these weapons. We could hear them practising shooting in the mountains around Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look into this. So on the 10th of July, 1990, you were mentioning this incident, a police patrol from Gacko noticed a truck passing close to Gacko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They tried to stop it and this was a patrol consisting of one Muslim and one Serb.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And they stopped the truck near the exit from the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They took the driver to the police station where they held him for a day or two, and then on the 12th of July, 50 cars full of people from Nevesinje arrived at the police station.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And set the driver free?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: In quotation marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And fired shots from automatic weapons I suppose into the air. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And they behaved in a wild manner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it clear that this is some sort of local smuggling of weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No. That's not clear, Mr. Milosevic. The Yugoslav army was arming the Serb population. It's true there was a mixed patrol consisting of Savo Stojanovic who was a Serb and the Kampala [phoen]. If this man was a Serb, it doesn't mean that he took part in this arming. It's true that they arrested the driver and brought him to Gacko and that on the 12th of July, and I think that this is an Orthodox holiday but I'm not sure, yes, yes. They came from Nevesinje, a column of cars to Gacko in front of the police. No one dared opposed them. They fired shots. They acted wildly, and then they took off the driver. He was from Nevesinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the driver was from Nevesinje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the other two participants were two policemen, one Serb and one Muslim who had nothing to do with it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the people from Nevesinje who came and behaved wildly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: These are all the participants in this event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What has that to do with this then, because that's the neighbouring municipality. There was a local arms smuggler, two local policemen. What has Serbia got to do with any of this? What has the JNA got to do with any of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Arms are not produced in Nevesinje or in Gacko. Weapons are produced in factories that in the former Yugoslavia were controlled by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, controlled by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: You could not go and buy weapons in a kiosk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Of course not. You're putting this in the context of the illegal arming and the paramilitary formations. Do you know that the first paramilitary formations set up in Bosnia and Herzegovina was the party, para-army of the SDA called the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I really don't know these dates. And this Patriotic League, was it a formation, a unit? What was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It was established all over Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: But not in Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Not in Gacko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember they had nine regional staffs, 103 municipal staffs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. That was at a higher level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that as part of these activities in August 1992, there were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Milosevic please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: -- battalions. Do you know all this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I don't know all this. I think this is pure propaganda.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're being asked to slow down, Mr. Milosevic, by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the leadership of this Patriotic League was entrusted to form a JNA officer, Sefer Halilovic, who was later appointed Commander-in-Chief of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and then to Lieutenant Colonel Meho Karisik --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has said he doesn't know anything about this. He describes it as propaganda. Whether it is or not we'll have to determine in due course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did these clashes, all the conflicts you are talking about, did they begin after the 6th of April, 1992, when the so-called international recognition of Bosnia and Herzegovina took place based on that rump referendum? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: You see, before this, the Muslim population in my municipality was mistreated. Two of our young men were killed. I think it was in March. Their names were Boskovic and Grebovic. People were beaten in Gacko. Their shops, the Muslim shops, were bombed. Muslim cafes were bombed. At that time, we were suffering under repression and mistreatment, so we didn't know much about what was going on outside our municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as you don't know anything further away from your municipality, do you know about the Green Berets, the directive given to the Green Berets and other Muslim formations that barracks and JNA officers and soldiers should be attacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No. This did not happen in Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You know that the Presidency of Yugoslavia, on the 4th of May, reached a decision that the JNA should withdraw from Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: What Presidency are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The Presidency of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I know about this. To what extent this was actually respected, that's a different matter. I think it was not, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you think today that it was a good thing for the JNA to withdraw from Bosnia and Herzegovina when all these paramilitaries were running amok in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: They were all part of the JNA. The White Eagles were part of the JNA, and all the other paramilitary units were part of the JNA. The JNA armed them. At least, they did in our area. That's what I saw and that's how I experienced it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The Muslim units and the HVO, they were also part of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: They weren't there in our area. These units weren't in our area. I can't talk about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I won't ask you about things you can't talk about. Just let me see. You say in paragraph 17 that "... this 'attacking battalion' were armed with automatic weapons, they held military exercises ... They were not dressed like soldiers at that time. In March 1991 there was a special police unit who had been sent to Bileca to calm the situation down when the weapons had been seized. When the police unit was on the way back to Sarajevo, the Serbs of the 'attacking battalion' and some other paramilitary units, led by Obren Govedarica, who was the head of the White Eagles for Herzegovina --" Let's stop here. This man whom I've just mentioned - and I was reading from your statement - is he from Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This unit of the White Eagles which you mention, were they also from Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: The attacking battalion is mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the White Eagles. You said at the beginning that in this -- during your testimony here. Were these White Eagles from Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: You see, their commander was a certain Ljubo, and a song was written about his heroism, his heroism in killing unarmed civilians during the attack on Kula, which is a Muslim village. This Ljubo was killed, Captain Ljubo, at that place, and a poem was written about his heroism saying he was born in Valjevo. That's what the song says. And this was published in 1992. It's a song written to be sung accompanied by the gusle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Govedarica, the commander of the White Eagles in Herzegovina, was a Herzegovinian and so were the members of the unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: What I meant when I said that -- well, Govedarica was not a military commander. He was the president of the regional committee for Herzegovina, and of course as a civilian commander, he had influence on the White Eagles, but their commander was Ljubo, and I think his last name was something like Moljevic or Mocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say Govedarica, leader of the White Eagles in Herzegovina. And then you say that the commander of the special police unit was named Vikic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He was a Serb too, was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I -- I added something to this. This is Dragan Vikic, and he was from the special unit of the republican MUP. So I'm not referring to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. MUP of Gacko but the republican MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But this Dragan Vikic has to be a Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No, he doesn't have to be a Serb. I don't know what he was. Dragan Vikic was one of the well-known commanders for the defence of Sarajevo. He's still living in Sarajevo, and he is an eminent person. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is what you say: "I think that in the case that this police unit did something contrary to what the Serbs wanted, the ambush would have shot at them."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So they didn't actually shoot, but you think that they would have shot had the other side done something they didn't like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. Why would they have rallied there otherwise, gathered there and set up an ambush in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, was it an ambush?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, they didn't do any shooting. Mr. Milosevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me if they shot or not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: It was like this, Mr. Milosevic: This man Obren Govedarica came to the municipality wearing a military uniform. He went to the president's office. That's where he was seen. He was our -- our representative was sitting there and when Obren came in and everybody knew each other there because you know what all that was about. It was the weapons seized from the Yugoslav army, from the national deputy named Kozic. The demonstrations ensued in Bileca and the republican MUP went to calm the situation down, and I think you know -- I think you know that it was all they could do to save their skins from Bileca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: From the specials of the republican MUP. And they escaped. Now, there was an ambush here as nothing happened in Bileca, as there was no shooting there, these here did not, but all that was coordinated and of course these people didn't have to shoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How do you say you -- to me that I should know? How should I know what was happening in another -- different republic in Gacko? What has Serbia got to do with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, I see that you have a lot of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I receive information when I have a witness, but I know nothing about Gacko to be quite frank.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: All right. But this is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then you say: "That day, I was sitting in Lazetic's office when Obren Govedarica entered right after that." That's the event you've just described. "He was dressed in regular JNA uniform without any insignia, he was full of enthusiasm, enthusiastic because he had managed to gather a large number of volunteers who were armed and ready for action." So these White Eagles that you're talking about under Obren Govedarica were local volunteers, in fact, who were now putting on the insignia of the White Eagles and didn't want to display their insignia of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Here it says "Serbs from the Assault Battalion and other paramilitary units including the White Eagles." That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So all these were in fact people from the ranks of the local population; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: It was like this: In the White Eagle units there were some local inhabitants, yes, there were, but the commander at the time was this man Ljubo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean the Ljubo who was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And when was he killed? In 1991, is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: He was killed during an attack on the Muslim village of Medjunici on the 17th of June, 1992. July, I'm sorry. I meant to say July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: So it was absolutely certain that he was within the White Eagles composition. They were from Serbia and I even sat with that man Ljubo with some municipal representatives. There was one of our men who had a political function there and he would often talk to these people. And then at this point this man Ljubo told the other one that he was the commander of the White Eagles and that he had the veterans, and I repeat, veterans from the Vukovar battlefield among its -- this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who organised that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, of course that was organised by the SDS and that there was this feedback mechanism that was set in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now you're talking about incidents that took place between the SDA and SDS, that is to say, between the Serbs and Muslims of your region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, but where is that here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's what you say in point 22, paragraph 22. Now, was it precisely in order to decrease tensions that the JNA had gone to Gacko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I'm not following you. Are you talking about the Muslims and the Serbs or the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about both the Muslims and the Serbs and the tension that existed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, my question is this: Was it precisely due to that tension that the JNA came to Gacko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: The JNA came to Gacko as it was withdrawing from Croatia and before that it was at the barracks at Bileca, that well-known barracks, and the Hercegovina Corps and units of the Uzice Corps were moving towards Mostar and I don't think that I can say that they came there to quell the situation. They came to perform quite another task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But at that time, the army of Republika Srpska was already in existence; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I do believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I hope -- are you not challenging that this was made up of soldiers and officers that were either born there or lived there before the war, the members of the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: The Republika Srpska army had -- well, we were expelled from Gacko at the time, but I do know that there were people from the area of Republika Srpska and from the broader area of Serbia as well, and Montenegro, and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Just explain this to me: You mentioned a moment ago the killing that took place in March 1992 of -- you say in March 1992, the White Eagles killed Zoran Grebovic who was from a Serb-Muslim marriage; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, but just tell me what paragraph that's in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I think it's paragraph 23 where you say that, but you know about all this. "On the 2nd of March, 1992, Serbian paramilitary units had a checkpoint in the direction of Foca. They stopped two Muslims who were returning from Foca, they took them with their car to the mountain called Cemerno and killed them."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Their names were Zoran Grebovic, who was from a mixed Serb-Muslim marriage, and Amir Poskovic, a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you go on to say who the killers are.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "... Mastilovic and Vukovic from Gacko. The bodies were discovered by a policeman," and all the rest of it, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore all this was taking place between the local Serbs and the local Muslims; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: This particular event was an event like that, yes, this specific event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, does that have anything to do with anyone from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Of course it does, because it was organised there. They had come to organise it. Ljubo had come to organise it. And I know on one occasion -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Haven't we just established that this event had nothing to do with people who weren't local Serbs or local Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes. We can accept that for this particular incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on now. You said a moment ago that the army, when it was withdrawing from Croatia, withdrew to your area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, among other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Where, where else could it have gone? It could have gone to Bosnia, to Serbia, to Montenegro. Where else could the army have gone if it had left Slovenia and left Croatia? Because it was on its own country's territory, the territory of its own state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is no need to answer that. Yes, Mr. Milosevic, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, this killing for which we established a moment ago was an incident which happened exclusively between local participants, and this disturbed people in Gacko a great deal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And that's quite understandable?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then you mention a meeting that was held -- actually, it was a large rally held with respect to that killing because the people were upset. And then you mention General Perisic, who came to attend the rally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No, Perisic didn't come to that rally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But the meeting held because of the incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Not even that, because the incident took place, I think, in March, the 5th of March -- the rally took place on the 5th of March, whereas the meeting with Perisic was on the 28th of April, in actual fact. So this isn't tied in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But it's tied into the situation, the general situation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: That's right, not meeting but the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what meeting was it that Perisic attended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: It was a party meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you attend the meeting yourself? Were you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, you don't have to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: This meeting was at a broader level, held at a broader level because the meeting was presided over by the president of the SAO of Herzegovina, and present were the representatives of the Serb municipalities from the area, from Stara Herzegovina, and several representatives by the Muslims from Gacko, I think, somebody along those lines. And the meeting was chaired by Milan Bojovic, the Prime Minister of the government of the Serb autonomous region of Herzegovina. And at the meeting the commander of the Yugoslav army was also present, and as far as I know, SAO Herzegovina was never a constitutional legal entity within Yugoslavia; it was in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It was a meeting at which Perisic attended, and did he say he was a commander in the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Which was composed of all the nations, all the ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: That was the story he told us but it wasn't a true story. That wasn't true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean it wasn't a true story? Wasn't the Yugoslav army composed of all the nations, all the ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: It was beforehand but not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But he emphasised that he would remain commander until all the three ethnic groups were there as part of the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He emphasised, therefore, he stressed that the Yugoslav army was an army of all the nations, all the ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And did he also say that he would prohibit paramilitary formations and their activities in his area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: That's what he said, but he didn't prohibit them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how much effort the JNA put in to place the paramilitaries under their control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, no. In my area, they gave logistic support to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know that Radovan Karadzic reacted with respect to the operations of the paramilitaries in Gacko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I'm not aware of that. I'd like to see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'll let you see an order here. I have an order.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, it's been translated into English, of the 3rd of July, 1992. That's the date of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The Presidency of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, at a meeting held on the 3rd of July, proclaimed an order to undertake an investigation on the activities of paramilitary groups in the area of the municipalities of Gacko and Nevesinje - which makes it your municipality and the neighbouring municipality - and it charges the Ministry of the Interior of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to conduct an investigation on the activities of paramilitary groups in the municipalities of Gacko and Nevesinje. And after the investigation, the ministry will table an extensive report with the facts established in the area of the two municipalities mentioned. The President of the Presidency, Dr. Radovan Karadzic. That's the signatory, and you can take a look at that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness have a look at the original, the B/C/S version, and we will have the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I -- I don't know -- I am not aware of this document, but it is quite obvious here that they were working in just one direction. At least that's my opinion, to start ethnic cleansing in Gacko which was to take place soon after this act, this document, Mr. Milosevic. I don't think that Mr. Karadzic considered Serb units to be paramilitaries. It is the Muslim civilian population here of an unarmed, empty-handed population. They considered that to be paramilitary organisations and that's where this is addressed to, because this was a forerunner. This preceded at, I would say, the best time to undertake preparations for ethnic cleansing in Gacko which began on the 17th of July of this same year, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. 1122. I really -- I've really heard a lot of things here, but can you really deduce from this document which states that the actions of paramilitary formations are to be established in the municipalities of Gacko and Nevesinje and you precisely said that there were no Muslim paramilitary formations, that this, in fact, refers to the Muslim and not to all paramilitary formations and that this, in fact, was addressed as an in -- as a set of instructions for ethnic cleansing. What are the grounds that you're able to state that on because you read it from start to finish? I read it out to you both these two points.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, this order is quite clear. I can see what it says, but I think that it is actually intended in quite a different direction, because I don't think that anybody looking around that -- that they would go on providing logistic support and support generally and be a component part of the armed forces unless that was the case. But one -- what was afoot here was that you had to invent an enemy and that there were Muslims somewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Wait a moment. There is an objection from Mr. Groome. Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would query the witness's ability to deal with the order. The order does refer to an extensive report. I would ask that that be placed before the witness if it is so available so that he may be able to more properly comment on what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He can deal with this. Of course he can. He can look Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. at it and he's made his comments on it. Now, Mr. Milosevic, your time is coming up. You've got two minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I should like to ask you to extent my time a little because I can't complete my cross-examination of this witness within the space of two minutes

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. What we'll do is this. We will take the break now. We will then give you ten minutes more and conclude the witness then. Do you want this document exhibited, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. It will be given the next D number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit 202, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now. Witness B-1122, you've heard there is another ten minutes cross-examination. There may be a few more minutes, a few more questions after that. Could you remember not to speak to anybody during this break until your evidence is over. Don't speak to anybody about it. Very well. We will adjourn now

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. 1122, please give brief replies to my questions because we have very little time. Is it true that General Perisic at that meeting agreed to your proposal that in order to protect the civilians joint patrols had to be established composed of one Muslim, one Serb, and one JNA soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And for paramilitaries to withdraw from the municipality? You even made a joint statement about that. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that several hundred Serbs gathered in front of the police station and that the JNA practically saved you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, Perisic promised this but it was never implemented, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear you properly. What did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: General Perisic promised these joint patrols but this was never actually implemented. It was just an empty promise. As for the arrests you mentioned on the 1st of June, it's true that in front of the police administration while the negotiations were going on there were several hundred people present. These were reservists, not paramilitaries. They were shooting in the air, drinking, running amok, and the Muslim negotiators were under enormous pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And did the army save you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: The army wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But nothing happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Well, that's when the arrests began, and they continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it true that on the 16th of April, 1992, you sent a message on behalf of the Muslim people of Gacko to the Territorial Defence Staff of Bosnia-Herzegovina where you say: "That the Muslim people of the municipality of Gacko on the day the TO of Bosnia and Herzegovina was established were put under command of that institution and please count on our full contribution and participation and all the tasks you entrust to us." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it's not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: What I'm saying is I'm not aware of the document. I'm not saying it's the not true, but I am not aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Is it true that in May 1992 sabotage was carried out in the thermonuclear -- thermoelectric plant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it was perpetrated by Zijad Mehic according to the investigation who destroyed a conveyer belt.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: It was not sabotage. I do know that a belt was damaged but not due to sabotage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And did this Mehic then flee to Fazlagica Kula near Gacko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: He didn't flee there, he lived there. It's the village of Kljuic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the attempts of the organs of law and order to bring him in were -- ended in shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: This is not correct. There was a patrol of some 20 armed men who went to that village purportedly to arrest him, but it was then that the shooting on Gacko started. So it's not true that they went to arrest him and that they were shot at. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in the meantime the Muslim part of the population withdrew to Fazlagica Kula and Borac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
utterances.text: Borac, yes that's true and one part remained in the town of Gacko. Mostly intellectuals who thought that nothing would happen, that they owed nothing to anyone and that nothing would happen. Later they were rounded up with their families, separated off, and atrocities were committed against their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at the time you're testifying about you had about 1.500 armed men in your ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1122
